title: MACH Factory Event v2
description: One transition of the intake ledger, as a line of .factory/intake/events.jsonl. Events are written only when the ledger changes, in sequence order, so the log can be replayed but is never a second source of truth.

seq.description: Strictly increasing by one; a reader resumes from the last seq it saw.

source_commit.description: The integration-branch commit the product definitions were read from.

runner_id.description: The machine-local runner that was enabled when this was written; null when the Factory was not enabled.

execution_id.description: The supervisor's execution this event belongs to, if any.

source.description: Which part of MACH acted: an engineer's command, product intake, or the supervisor.

cause.description: The seq of the event that led to this one, where one is known.

refs.description: Where the authoritative state is kept, as paths in the project: the cell's cell.json, the execution's folder. An event describes a change; these say where to read the truth.

data.description: Details by type: problems (intake.refused), reasons (dependency.blocked), depends_on (dependency.resolved), commit (slice.integrated), stage, risk, branch, by (engineer, or the name of an authorized caller) and authorization (work.scheduled), from_revision and effect (revision.superseded), reason (human.required). Supervisor events: autonomy, limits and by (factory.*); from_commit and commit (revision.discovered); dispatched, started and held (scheduling.decided); stage, next and attempt (work.claimed); session_id, workflow, until and limits, and since M6.5 provenance (a snapshot of digests, versions and identifiers taken once at start, or null with provenance_reason capture-failed; see M6_1_EVENT_CONTRACT.md section 10.1.1) (execution.started); from_stage and stage (station.observed); kind (recovery.started); stage, next, waiting_for, how, seen_to_end and cost_usd (execution.completed); how, claude_error, exit_code and attempt (execution.failed). Never a prompt, a command line, an environment variable or a credential.
